# About Chess Trainer

[Português (Brasil)](ABOUT.pt-BR.md) · [Español](ABOUT.es.md)

## Who made it

I am Nielsen Campos: a data and backend engineer, a semi-professional musician (almost amateur) and an amateur chess player (and I think that is where it stops, or maybe not, who knows 😂).

## The project

Chess Trainer is a simple place to study for players who teach themselves. It started as a single page to drill my own openings and grew into a place to train in general, to learn without a real instructor and even without playing over the board.

Its advantages: your study stays on your own computer, not online, so your preparation stays private, as grandmasters keep theirs today. Nothing leaves it unless you import your games from a site. And it costs nothing: just run it and use it.

It does not replace courses, learning platforms or instructors. It is only a help for amateur, beginner and semi-professional players.

## Who paved my way

In chronological order, the people, books and platforms that brought me here.

1. **Henrique Mecking (Mequinho)**: Brazilian grandmaster, once third in the world. I have been learning chess from the book Mequinho: o xadrez de um grande mestre since 1991. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrique_Mecking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrique_Mecking)
1. **Chessmaster**: The best-selling series of chess video games, today Ubisoft's. I started playing it in 2001, on the SNES and the PC. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chessmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chessmaster)
1. **Antonio Radić (agadmator)**: Croatian YouTuber whose channel goes through famous games; in 2021 he was the first chess creator to pass a million subscribers. On his channel I started watching chess and getting to know the great masters, and in 2014 I started playing online. [youtube.com/@agadmator](https://www.youtube.com/@agadmator)
1. **Lichess**: A free and open-source chess site, with no ads, run by a non-profit. Where I started playing, because of agadmator. [lichess.org](https://lichess.org/)
1. **Levy Rozman (GothamChess)**: American International Master, author and creator, known as "the Internet's chess teacher". I have followed him since 2020. He helped me understand strategy in more depth, get to know the people of the chess world and move to Chess.com for good. His course is on Chessly, and his book is How to Win at Chess. [youtube.com/@GothamChess](https://www.youtube.com/@GothamChess) · [chessly.com](https://chessly.com/)
1. **Chess.com**: The largest chess site in the world. Where I moved because of Levy, and where I kept learning more about chess. [chess.com](https://www.chess.com/) · [youtube.com/@chess](https://www.youtube.com/@chess) · [youtube.com/@chesscomPT](https://www.youtube.com/@chesscomPT) · [youtube.com/@ChesscomES](https://www.youtube.com/@ChesscomES)
1. **Evandro Barbosa**: Brazilian grandmaster and creator, with whom I have been learning to plan since 2023, also through his course platform, Chessflix. [youtube.com/@GMEvandroBarbosa](https://www.youtube.com/@GMEvandroBarbosa) · [chessflix.com.br](https://chessflix.com.br/)
1. **Hikaru Nakamura**: American grandmaster, five-time U.S. champion, 2022 Fischer Random world champion, one of the best players in the world and one of its biggest streamers. I found him through Levy around 2024, and learned a lot from him about memorization. His style reminds me of Tal's, the Magician from Riga. [youtube.com/@GMHikaru](https://www.youtube.com/@GMHikaru)
1. **Krikor Mekhitarian**: Brazilian grandmaster and creator, Brazilian champion in 2012 and 2015, who played five Chess Olympiads for Brazil. From him I have been learning tactics since around 2024, also through his courses on openings and more. With WIM Flor, he hosts Chess.com's broadcasts in Portuguese on YouTube. [youtube.com/@GMKrikor](https://www.youtube.com/@GMKrikor) · [gmkrikor.com.br](https://gmkrikor.com.br/)

## Other legends and references

- **Alexandra & Andrea Botez**: Canadian sisters who host BotezLive, one of the best-known chess channels, mixing chess and entertainment. Alexandra is a Woman FIDE Master and played three Women's Chess Olympiads for Canada. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_Botez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_Botez) · [youtube.com/@BotezLive](https://www.youtube.com/@BotezLive)
- **Anatoly Karpov**: World champion from 1975 to 1985, and FIDE champion again from 1993 to 1999, famous for his positional play. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoly_Karpov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoly_Karpov)
- **Daniel Naroditsky (Danya)**: In memoriam. American grandmaster, author and commentator, and one of the best chess teachers on YouTube. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Naroditsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Naroditsky) · [youtube.com/@DanielNaroditskyGM](https://www.youtube.com/@DanielNaroditskyGM)
- **Eric Rosen**: American International Master and streamer, known for his traps, the Stafford Gambit and his calm "Oh no, my queen!". [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Rosen_(chess_player)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Rosen_(chess_player)) · [youtube.com/@EricRosen](https://www.youtube.com/@EricRosen)
- **Garry Kasparov**: World champion from 1985 to 2000, and number one in the world for about twenty years. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_Kasparov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_Kasparov)
- **Hans Niemann**: American grandmaster since 2021 and streamer, one of the strongest young players of his generation. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Niemann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Niemann)
- **Josh Waitzkin**: American chess prodigy, twice U.S. junior champion, whose childhood inspired the film Searching for Bobby Fischer. He later became a martial arts world champion and wrote The Art of Learning. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Waitzkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Waitzkin)
- **Judit Polgár**: Hungarian grandmaster, considered the strongest woman player in history. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judit_Polgár](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judit_Polg%C3%A1r)
- **Luis Paulo Supi**: Brazilian grandmaster since 2018 and three-time Brazilian champion. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Paulo_Supi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Paulo_Supi) · [youtube.com/@GMLuisPauloSupi](https://www.youtube.com/@GMLuisPauloSupi)
- **Magnus Carlsen**: Norwegian, world champion from 2013 to 2023 and the highest-rated player in history. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnus_Carlsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnus_Carlsen)
- **Maria Florencia Fernández (Flor)**: Argentine Woman International Master (WIM), five-time Argentine women's champion. With Krikor, she hosts Chess.com's broadcasts in Portuguese. [pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Florencia_Fernandez](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Florencia_Fernandez)
- **Mikhail Tal**: World champion in 1960, the Magician from Riga, famous for his sacrifices and attacks. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Tal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Tal)
- **Rafael Leitão**: Brazilian grandmaster, seven-time Brazilian champion, also a correspondence chess grandmaster (ICCF), who teaches on his channel. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Leitão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Leit%C3%A3o) · [youtube.com/@gmrafaelleitao](https://www.youtube.com/@gmrafaelleitao)
- **Robert Fischer (Bobby)**: American, world champion from 1972 to 1975 after beating Spassky in the Match of the Century, and the creator of Chess960 (Fischer Random). [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Fischer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Fischer)
- **Roberto Molina**: Brazilian International Master, Brazilian champion in 2018. In 2021 he beat Levy in the final of the I'm Not A GM Speed Chess Championship. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Junio_Brito_Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Junio_Brito_Molina)
- **Shakhriyar Mamedyarov**: Azerbaijani grandmaster and his country's highest-rated player, whose best rating, 2820, is among the highest in history. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakhriyar_Mamedyarov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakhriyar_Mamedyarov)
- **Vasyl Ivanchuk**: Ukrainian grandmaster since 1988, three times number two in the world, known for his creativity and for playing almost any opening. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasyl_Ivanchuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasyl_Ivanchuk)
- **Viswanathan Anand**: Indian, his country's first grandmaster and world champion from 2007 to 2013. [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viswanathan_Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viswanathan_Anand)
